Three things beyond the Fischer swap.

Start Gaborik's line against their third pair. Fortin is 66 overall, Belak is 68. That's the biggest gap on their blue line and Gaborik at 99 speed will burn them every shift he gets.

Press Witt. He's got PUCK 64 and DEKG 55 -- he's not comfortable with the puck in his own end. Your forecheck should target him specifically. If he's turning it over, Gonchar has to come over to help and that opens the other side.

Don't touch your PK. Their PP is 12 for 122, which is 9.8%. Whoever is on that unit tonight doesn't matter against that.

One faceoff note: Sundin at 89 wins the draw against Lang at 66 all night. Richards at 75 loses his to Halpern at 85. If it's a tight game late and you need a defensive draw, Richards is the one to pull for Chlup at 78.

That's the lot. The rest is just not playing behind the play early.
Okay, I understand. And a good point about swapping Fischer left to my jogger speed. Any other tips strategy-wise?

I mapped the deadline market against the coach's two gaps, because with 63 days to March 19 and 12 points clear, we are buyers and the window is open now. The answer is three packages that stack without overlapping assets. Lead: Belfour plus our first-rounder to Ottawa for Chara (88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 27, $1.70M expiring) and Havlat (61 pts, 23, $0.90M). That closes toughness from 72 to 88 and adds top-six scoring. Second: Chistov plus the Detroit second to Atlanta for Kovalchuk (78 pts at 21) and ask for Savard (89 FACE) folded in. Third: Holden plus a third-rounder to Pittsburgh for Abid (56 pts, 80 TOUG, $400K). Net payroll saving if all three land: $4.70M. Separately, Gaborik at 67 points and $1.10M expiring needs a six-year deal this month, not in July.

Put them both in for Monday. Washington is 23-14-5 with Kolzig at 93 in net, nothing like the garbage teams we've been resting people against. Nash at 0.88 per game and Spacek at 0.61 are exactly the depth you need when the goalie is that good and they've got Jagr at 89 and Bondra at 86 up front. I'd be comfortable leaving them out against a 5-18 team but not this one.

Beyond Monday, I understand the logic. You're building two groups of young players and someone has to sit. I just need to know ahead of time so I can build lines around who's actually there instead of guessing.

I was giving some other players space so I scratched Nash and Spaček because I wanted some other young players to have some playtime so they can develop properly but if you think that for Washington it is the right choice to go all out I will reinstigate Nash and Spaček

Nothing has changed since my last two messages. Belfour starts Monday, Fischer swaps to left D to match Jagr's speed, no other matchup changes. Their PP at 9.8% is noise. I still have no word on Nash or Spacek and won't ask again; if they're healthy they go in, if not I work around it.

Still waiting on Nash and Spacek. Monday is two days out and I can't build lines around players I don't know the status of. If they're healthy, Nash at 0.88 pts/g and Spacek at 0.67 belong in; if something's keeping them out, tell me and I'll work around it. Everything else for Washington stays as I left it: Belfour starts, no matchup changes, their 9.8% PP is noise.

Monday in Washington. I went through whether this matchup asks anything our current lines can't handle, and it doesn't. Their PP is 12 for 122, 9.8%, so PK personnel is irrelevant. Gaborik at 99 speed against their second pair at 75 overall is the mismatch we exploit. Belfour starts, no matchup changes.

What does need fixing has nothing to do with Washington. Nash has 30 points in 34 games and is scratched. Spacek is 19 with a 0.61 rate and is also sitting. Spezza is at 7.8 minutes with morale 86 and his development window is closed at this usage. I'm moving him to third-line centre for 12+ tonight. Tucker (checking 88, toughness 84) goes over Koltsov (checking 55, worst on the roster) on that left wing. Chlup slides to fourth. These are development and role calls, not matchup ones, and they should happen against anyone.

Marcus Bell, The Tunnel. Could I have ten minutes on the record about the front office?

TOR are 33-8-1, 73 points in 45.

Reply /call when you are free and I will ring you. /no if not today.

Monday at Washington, I checked whether we need to adjust anything. We don't. Their PP is 9.8% so PK personnel is irrelevant, Sundin at FACE 89 beats their first-line draw man at 66, and our third and fourth lines are deeper than theirs. Belfour starts -- their power shooting (Jagr SHPW 95, Gonchar SHPW 93) suits his BRKA 95 and REBC 94 better than Tellqvist at 75.

The real business is the lineup. Nash at 0.88 pts/g and 30 points in 34 games is sitting. Put him back in. Spezza is at 5.7 MPG and 0.38 pts/g with morale 86, the room's lowest. I asked for 12 minutes on January 8 and it didn't happen. If it doesn't happen this week the window on that kid closes for good. Upshall's rate fell below 0.55, so the signal from January 8 is gone. He stays as-is but don't expect more from him.

Got it -- writing it up now.
[voice note, 33s]

Ed, you said you're not really buying this year, and then in the same breath you said you might need someone to bring toughness. Those two things pull against each other. If you find the right body before March, is the cap room you just told me about enough to absorb him?
[voice note, 51s]

Ed, you're the only club in the league with nobody on the injured list right now, 33 and 8, plus 131 on the season. At the trade deadline, are you a buyer looking to add for a long playoff run, or are you so happy with what's in that building that you just ride this group?
[voice note, 45s]

Ed, you're looking at $66.97 million in payroll right now, and you've just said you want to keep Marian and Brad and Ed and most of the guys. You're ninth in the league on cost per point at $0.92 million. Does that number give you the room to do all of that, or does someone eventually have to take a haircut?
[voice note, 58s]

Ed, you said you're offering continuing deals to Marian and Brad, and now you're telling me Nash is already top-six. That's a young core right there. When July opens, is Gaborik the first call you make before the market sets his price, or is this a room where nobody jumps the queue?
[voice note, 20s]

Ed, you said you're lucky to have the young talent in your building. Rick Nash is 20, 17 goals in 34 games, up 5 on the Index. Is he already a top-six forward for you, or are you still developing him at his own pace?
[voice note, 14s]

Ed, you mentioned the bottom line depends on how the older guys are feeling. Gary Roberts is 38, Svehla is 36, and both are on one year. Are you planning to bring them back at a reduced number, or is the club ready to let that group walk and make room for the younger core?
[voice note, 55s]
Ed, you say the questions about Belfour are misplaced, and fair enough, he's got a 2.42 GAA and five shutouts. But Aebischer is 26 and has 15 wins in 19 games. Come October, who is your number one?
[voice note, 69s]

Ed, Marcus Bell, The Tunnel, calling from the desk in Toronto. You've got five players on one-year deals and three of them are the core of this team, so I wanted to talk about where this roster is going come July. Got a minute?

Ed, Marian Gaborik is 22 years old, a 97 overall, up six on the Bureau's Development Index, and he's on one year and $1.10 million. Brad Richards is 24, a contract year, $1.00 million. Ed Belfour is 39, a contract year, $6.50 million. How do you sort that room in the summer?

Monday away at Washington. I went through whether their shape demands a lineup change, and it does not. Roberts at 86 checking already shadows Jagr at 52 checking and 62 toughness. Sundin wins the draw against their first centre 89 to 66. Their blue line from position three down reads 66-75 overall. Our speed eats them. Belfour starts. Their power play converts under 10% (12 on 122).

The real news is back home. Nash at 30 points in 34 games at 20 is sitting. I am putting him back on the second line. Spezza at 7.8 minutes with morale down to 86 needs 12+. Spacek went from 16 minutes to 10.2 while his rate climbed from 0.55 to 0.67. My error, correcting it. Safronov has played 3 games all season and I cannot fix that from the bench. You need to tell me if he is in or out.

I checked what the deadline market gives us for toughness and faceoffs, because the roster has zero players above 73 base TOUG and Sundin at 90 FACE is the only draw man above 80. Three packages are ready: Belfour plus our 1st for Chara and Havlat from OTT (88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 61 pts from Havlat), the DET 2nd plus Chistov for Kovalchuk (78 pts, 21, $1.10M), and the 3rd plus Holden for Abid (87 TOUG, 56 pts, $400K). They do not overlap in assets and save $4.80M combined. New find: Savard at 89 FACE and 48 pts on ATL should fold into the Kovalchuk talk at no extra cost. Separately, Chlup at 18 with POTE 95 needs a 5-6 year extension before his price moves. The deadline is March; we are 12 points clear, so the posture is buy.

I mapped the full seller board for March because the toughness gap (zero players above 73) is the only hole that costs us a series, and the window to fill it closes on March 4th. Three proposals stack and use different assets. First: Belfour plus our own first-rounder to OTT for Chara (90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 46 pts, 28, $1.70M expiring) and Havlat (86 ovr, 61 pts, $900K). OTT are 15-21-4 with 11 expiring deals. Second: DET second-rounder plus Chistov to ATL for Kovalchuk (80 pts, 22, $1.10M). Third: third-rounder plus Holden to PIT for Abid (86/86 toughness and checking, 54 pts, 25, $400K). All three can land simultaneously and save $4.80M net. Belfour moves either way; open the OTT conversation first.

I checked whether the deadline market can fix our two real holes, toughness at a 73 ceiling and faceoffs carried by Sundin alone at 90, because the deadline is early March and the sellers are still selling. Chara (OTT, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 80 ovr, $1.70M expiring, 45 pts/41 GP) is confirmed; OTT sit 15-20-4 with 11 expiring deals. Kovalchuk (ATL, 92, 78 pts/41 GP, 21, $1.10M expiring) is the ceiling play with the own first-rounder plus Koltsov. Heatley (91 base, 74 pts/38 GP, same ATL deal) is the pivot if ATL keep Kovalchuk. Belfour should go for a pick before March; 39, $6.50M, expiring. Chlup extension is the most urgent contract on the sheet: 18, POTE 95, $2.34M, two years left. Lock him this month before another 15 points erases his price.

The December package agreed on the 22nd has sat for nineteen days without executing, and I found a target that changes who we call first. Thornton at Boston is real: 91 overall, 82 toughness, 80 faceoffs, 66 points in 40 games, $4.00M expiring. Boston are 15-19-3 with 13 expiring deals. He is the single best player on the deadline board and fixes faceoffs, toughness, and centre depth in one body. I dismissed him on January 5th because I had the wrong player. Chara at Ottawa (80 ovr, 88/89 TOUG/CHKG, 45 pts in 41 GP, $1.70M expiring) is now confirmed as a seller too at 15-19-4 with 11 expiring. Priority: execute the December package this week, open the Thornton conversation in February, and move Belfour, Svehla, and Roberts for picks before March. Aebischer at 2.62 GAA and .898 in 19 starts is ready for the crease.

Pittsburgh Sunday, 3-0-0 against them and their PP converts at 13.0%, so no matchup changes. What I did is fix the lineup for development. Nash goes in on the third line over Chistov: Nash has 30 points in 34 games at 0.88 a night and keeps getting scratched while Chistov sits there producing 0.33 in 27 games. Spezza moves to third-line centre from the fourth; he is at 8.4 minutes and morale dropped 4 to 89, and at 21 with a climbing rate he needs 12 plus or his window closes. Colaiacovo needs to play every night on the second pair, not 49 percent of games. Belfour starts. Chlup gets PK2 reps tonight since their PP is toothless and he needs NHL experience at 18. Safronov is still your problem to solve, dress him or move him, his morale just dropped 5.

Can this roster survive next July, and what do we do before March to make sure it does? That was the job. Short answer: yes, but only if three things happen. First, close the December package. It moves toughness from a ceiling of 73 base to 91 and 94 through Jackman and Sutton, adds Sillinger at 91 faceoffs, and costs nothing from our own first-rounder. STL at 8-23-3, PHX at 15-21-4, ATL at 8-18-2 are all selling. Second, extend Chlup now. He is 18, $2.34M, POTE 95, 22 points in 30 games, and every top-nine season erases that price. Third, move Belfour for a pick before March. He is 39, $6.50M, expiring, and the above-80 mechanic means we get a draft choice or we get nothing in July. Aebischer at 2.62 and 0.898 is ready. One correction the coach should know: Tucker's 92 toughness was a form spike over a 70 base. The gap is worse than his report suggested.

I checked whether the January 4 Chara-Thornton renegotiation holds up against current data, because that is what sits on the negotiation table right now. It does not. Chara is 78 overall on a .457 Ottawa club, not a seller, and no Thornton on any roster reads 92 overall and 37 points. Retire that proposal; the original December 22 package stays as fallback.

The real deadline board: Kovalchuk (ATL, 92 ovr, 69 points in 38 games, $1.10M expiring, club at 11-21-2) is the top target. Bell (CHI, 89 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $0.90M, two years left) solves the toughness gap at a third-rounder. Bouwmeester (FLA, 21, POTE 96, expiring) is the keeper.

Summer: lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, and Chlup on five-to-six year deals before February ends. Belfour goes at the March deadline for a pick.

Friday's Boston game needs no adjustment. They have no defenceman above 74 and Raycroft at 77 in net — our current speed mismatches already exploit them. What matters more is who's sitting at home while producing. Nash is out with 30 points in 34 games, Eminger is out with 15 in 30, Colaiacovo is out with 11 in 19. That's the fourth time since late December a young regular has gone from dressing to watching while his rate was climbing. I'm putting all three back. Spezza needs a real run too — 14 points on 8.3 minutes a night, morale at 88, rate climbing from 0.43 to 0.62. He's stalling on the bench. One line change: Tucker for Koltsov on the third line. Koltsov at 0.42 on 9.6 failed the threshold we set December 20, and Tucker's 81 checking gives L3 a structural job it doesn't currently have. Two things I can't fix with a lineup: we have no centre above 89 in faceoffs besides Sundin, and no shutdown pair behind McCabe and Fischer. Those are deadline problems.

You're right, I got that wrong. Mogilny is back and fit — he returned today, January 5th, and he's lined on the first line right wing for Friday. My mistake, I misread it. He's in the lineup, Sundin down the middle, Roberts on the left. Nothing changes there.
Wtf, mogilny is not injured

Mogilny is out tonight with a lower-body injury returning January 5th, so I went through who fills his spot and whether NJ's physicality forces anything else. They start Schwab at 76 overall, we're 2-0-0 against them with 12 goals to 2, and Belfour stays in net. Alexeev moves to L1 right wing for the one night, Tucker dresses and takes Mogilny's penalty-kill spot permanently from here. But the bigger thing: Nash, Spezza, Eminger and Colaiacovo are all still scratched after being flagged December 29th. Nash has 30 points in 34 games at 20. Spezza's morale dropped 4 points to 88 because he's sitting on 8 minutes a night with 14 points in 29. Eminger broke out to 1.00 points per game on the first pair and Fischer is at 0.15 on 21. I am putting all four in tonight. This is the lineup construction problem I warned about and it's getting worse, not better.

I checked whether the deadline market has changed since we agreed the three-deal package on December 22, because it hasn't executed and we have 60 days.

It has changed. Two targets are better than what we agreed. Thornton (92 ovr, 62 pts in 37 games, 83 TOUG, 81 FACE, $4.00M expiring on a 37-point club) fills toughness, faceoffs, and scoring in one move. Chara (82 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 44 pts in 38 games, $1.70M expiring) is strictly better than Sutton on every axis. Both sit on sellers with 13 expiring deals each.

I would propose Mogilny plus the DET first-rounder for Thornton, Koltsov plus our second-rounder for Chara, and Belfour for a pick regardless of either. Keep Jackman and the original package as the fallback if those stall.

Separately: Tucker at 83 checking is still unlined. Line him tonight, it costs nothing.

I checked whether NJ forces a lineup change Monday. They don't. We won the first meeting 8-1 on this construction, our speed beats theirs on three of four lines, and Gaborik at 99 speed against Rafalski's 65 checking is a free matchup. Belfour starts.

The problem is internal. Nash has 30 points in 34 games and is scratched. Eminger is at 1.00 pts/g on 20 minutes and is scratched. Spezza's morale just dropped 4 to 88 sitting on the bench. I want Nash in on a top-six wing, Eminger on the first pair (Fischer at 0.15 is done), Upshall back to 13 minutes, and Chlup on the first PK replacing Mogilny. Those are the calls. Koltsov at 0.42 is below the threshold we set -- he's a trade candidate now. Faceoff gap still unsolvable within the roster.

The deadline is eight weeks out, the December package still has not executed, and I checked whether anything changes the plan. One new move: Belfour.

Execute the three agreed deals. Mogilny plus our second to STL for Jackman (90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, $0.70M), our third to PHX for Sillinger (96 FACE), Safronov plus our fourth to ATL for Sutton (92 TOUG, 88 CHKG). Toughness rises from 73 to 90/92. Faceoffs go from Sundin alone at 90 to Sundin alongside Sillinger at 96.

Belfour is the new call. 39 years old, 91 overall, $6.50M, CONS 50. Above 80 and not re-signing means he can move for a pick before March. Aebischer is ready: 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV, 15-3 in 19 starts.

Chlup needs five to six years on paper now. 18, POTE 95, $2.34M, two years left. His price changes after a full top-nine season.

Summer carries 17 contracts worth $28.60M expiring at once. Lock Gaborik (56 pts), Richards (43), Nash (30), Kaberle on five to six years; everyone else two to three so the next cluster hits in 2007.

The question I set out to answer: why are we scratching four young players who are producing while the aging top six slows down? Against Vancouver on Friday, the matchup itself needs nothing from us -- Roberts and Sundin are built to handle Bertuzzi, and Gaborik feasts on their 65-rated third pair. But our lines are wrong for a different reason. Nash (30 points in 34 games, 0.88 per game) has been out seven days since his injury cleared. Spezza (14 in 29, 21 years old) has sat 19 days. Eminger (15 points in 30 at 16 minutes) is a healthy scratch. All three need to be in the lineup. I'm also pulling Mogilny off the penalty kill -- he's 35, he's on three situations, and at 74 checking he adds nothing to what Roberts (81) and Fischer (82) already do there. Belfour starts at 92. Fischer at 0.15 points per game on 21 minutes is past the recovery window and I want him off the top pair.

Can this roster win a playoff series, and what has to happen between now and March to protect the next three years? The answer: the three-deal package agreed on the 22nd still hasn't executed, and Mogilny is at 0.60 pts/g on 17.6 minutes, down from his first-line rate. Every game he cools, STL's offer shrinks. Execute it. The Sillinger and Sutton deals go in parallel; combined they cut payroll $2.56M and fix the two structural holes the coach flagged: toughness 73 to 92, faceoffs 90 to 96.

Tucker lines up tonight, free. He carries 83 checking, 92 toughness, and sits unlined.

Two new targets worth building toward: Frolov from LA (22, 40 pts, POTE 96, $1.10M) as the Mogilny replacement for Holden plus Koltsov, and Avery from LA (94 FACE, $0.40M, two years) for a late pick. The summer cluster is the bigger threat: 17 deals, $28.6M, all expiring at once. Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, and Chlup on five-to-six before the season ends.

Package check before March: does the three-deal plan still hold, and has anything better surfaced since we agreed it five days ago? It holds. Jackman (90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, 3yr $0.70M), Sillinger (96 FACE, $1.80M expiring), Sutton (92/88, 4yr $1.34M) take toughness from 73 to 90 and the faceoff column from Sundin alone to two men. Net minus-2.56M payroll. One addition: Abid for Koltsov. Abid has 42 pts in 35 GP at 87/87 physical grades for 400K; PIT at 10-17-5 are sellers and his deal expires. Koltsov has collapsed to 0.38 pts/g on 6.2 minutes and the coach wants a decision within two weeks. He is surplus. Also worth a fifth-rounder: Avery at LA, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, $400K, 4 pts in 35 games. A pure specialist who solves both gaps cheaply. Dress Tucker tonight; his 92 checking and 88 toughness are the best internal mitigation while these deals sit unexecuted.

You're right, my mistake. It's December 27th, the deadline is March, so we're roughly 75 days out. I kept saying "this week" and that was wrong — the three-deal package (Jackman for Mogilny and a second, Sillinger for a third, Sutton for Safronov and a fourth) was agreed on the 22nd but hasn't executed, and none of it is urgent right now. STL are 8-20-2 and still selling, PHX at 13-18-4, ATL at 8-20-2. The market isn't going anywhere by February. The window to make these calls is January and early March, not today.

The thing that is worth doing right now is dressing Tucker and giving Koltsov and Spacek every night — that's the coach's call, not a trade.
The dealdine is not this week what are you talking about? This is december!

The three-deal package agreed on 22 December has not executed. The roster still shows Mogilny, no Jackman, no Sillinger, no Sutton. STL are now 8-20-2 and still selling, PHX at 13-18-4 with 14 expiring contracts, ATL at 8-20-2 still rebuilding. The market has not moved but Mogilny's value only falls from here and the deadline is roughly 64 days out. These three trade screens need to go out this week. Separately, Tucker at 83 CHKG, 88 TOUG, 29 years old, is in the press box while a 35-year-old is on the first penalty kill. Dress him tonight, no cost. The summer plan is built: $14.80M walks in July across Belfour, Svehla, Roberts and Renberg, and the four core pieces go on five-year deals. No further moves beyond what's above unless Cammalleri comes available.

The three-deal package is locked and the deadline plan is done, so I went looking for what else the market offers beyond it. LA is the answer. Cammalleri at 83 overall, 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring from a 9-16-5 club is the best value left in the league. He replaces Mogilny's wing with five years of runway instead of six weeks of rental. The offer I'd make: Holden (26, $1.20M, 0 GP) plus the Detroit first. Payroll nets minus $0.10M. If LA wants two picks, the DET first is the one to spend; the TOR round-0 stays in reserve for summer. Belfour is the other call: keep him through June for the playoff run, let him walk in July, or move him for a pick now and trust Aebischer's 19 starts. Tellqvist at .865 in seven games is not a backup for April. The summer cluster (17 deals, $28.6M) is planned and ready for July.

Deadline is this week and we are first in the East at 56 points, so the question was what the market gives us for the two holes the coach flagged. Three deals close both: Mogilny and our second-rounder to STL for Jackman, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, three years at $0.70M; our third-rounder to PHX for Sillinger, FACE 96, expiring rental; Safronov and a fourth to ATL for Sutton, 92 TOUG, four years at $1.34M. All three fill roles we have zero depth at, and combined they cut payroll $2.56M. The Detroit first stays untouched. If Jackman stalls, dress Tucker tonight and chase Wanvig at MIN for a fourth. Separately, lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Kaberle on five-year deals now, not in July; their current combined $5.20M will not survive another 30 games at this production.

Tuesday's game against STL (8-17-2, giving up 4.0 a night) is the easiest we get this month, so it's the night to rest and develop without risking a result.

Starting Belfour. Aebischer is at 80 morale, lowest on the roster, and STL's power play converts at 10 percent with their goalie at 81. Zero downside.

Moving Nash up to the second line. He's at 0.91 points per game in 13 minutes at age 20, best rate on the roster outside Gaborik. He's earned top-nine ice and tonight's soft matchup is the place to try it.

Putting Koltsov back in over Upshall. Koltsov is producing 0.78 per game in 6 minutes; Upshall is at 0.41 in 14. Koltsov's been benched for no production reason.

Mogilny comes off the first penalty kill for Tucker (79 checking, 68 toughness). Nothing else changes.

I scanned the full league for what fills our two uncovered roles — toughness (zero players at 80+) and faceoffs (only Sundin at 90 above 80) — and the deadline board gives us three targets that together cost less than we spend today.

Jackman (90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 83 ovr, 23, $0.70M, 3yr) from STL is the toughness buy. Mogilny plus our second-rounder is the price.

Sutton from ATL is new: 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 76 ovr, 27, $1.34M, four years. ATL are 8-18-2 rebuilding around Bouwmeester. Safronov plus a fourth-rounder gets him and solves the coach's Safronov problem before his morale drops further.

Sillinger (96 FACE, 88 ovr, 33, $1.80M expiring) from PHX is the faceoff rental for the spring. Third-rounder.

All three: payroll drops $2.56M, toughness goes from 73 to 90 and 92, faceoffs go from one option to two. I need your go-ahead on the Sutton-Safronov match specifically because the coach wants that call made this week.

Tonight's question was whether TB's shape demands any adjustment. It doesn't -- their best defenceman is Boyle at 75, Lecavalier's faceoff is 60 so Sundin at 88 wins that draw all night, and they're not physical enough to test our checking gap. Play the lines as they are, start Aebischer (84, 86 speed for their transition).

What I need from you is Safronov. He's at 95 morale, down 5 last save with 1 game in 32. I'm dressing him tonight on the third pair, but if that doesn't fix it within two weeks he goes on the block at his current value -- 91 scouting number, still tradeable at 95 morale. At 80s he's costing 1 point per grade and nobody wants him.

Two development moves: Koltsov up to third-line left wing over Chistov (0.78 points per game on 7.6 minutes versus Chistov's 0.39 on 10.2). Alexeev to second-line centre (19 points in 32 games on fourth-line minutes, that's top-six production buried). Neither breaks chemistry on a winning unit.

I went through the deadline market for our two holes, toughness and faceoffs, because at 24-6-0 we should be buying and not waiting for a hole to cost us a series.

Toughness: zero players at 80+ TOUG on our roster. Jackman (STL, 83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, three years at $0.70M) is the fix. The package shifts from a second-round pick alone to Mogilny plus a second. Mogilny's 95 overall and 42 points in 28 games still price him as first-round weight, and STL at 8-17-2 need scoring for their rebuild more than they need $5.50M.
